CIV.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~1850 kt (recovered from drought-hit ~1674 kt in 2023/24). World's #1 grower (~38% of global). Domestic grindings ~800 kt; balance of beans exported raw — NLD, MYS, DEU, BEL, TUR, USA largest destinations.

GHA.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~600 kt, up from crisis-low ~530 kt in 2023/24. World's #2 grower. Cocobod markets the crop; beans flow mainly to EU, USA, Malaysia, Turkey; domestic grindings ~220 kt.

ECU.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~480 kt, up from ~430 kt. Fastest-rising major; Anecacao reported 2024 cocoa export earnings ~US$3.3-3.6bn (+156% y/y on price spike). Top bean destinations: USA, Indonesia, NLD, Malaysia.

NGA.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~350 kt (~7% of world). Almost all beans exported; NLD, Malaysia, Belgium, Germany main buyers. Limited domestic grinding.

CMR.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~320 kt (~7% of world). Beans flow heavily to the Netherlands and Turkey, with some local grinding.

IDN.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~200 kt but grindings ~480 kt — a major Asian processor that now imports more beans than it grows. WITS 2024 gross bean imports ~157 kt (Ecuador, Cote d'Ivoire, PNG, Nigeria, Peru).

BRA.note: ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25: prod ~210 kt, grindings ~240 kt. Brazil consumes essentially all it grows and imports modest volumes in deficit years; not a significant bean exporter.

NLD.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Netherlands gross bean imports 817.6 kt (world's largest importer) — Cote d'Ivoire 292.6, Cameroon 144.5, Nigeria 143.9, Ghana 41.9, Ecuador 40.3. Europe's top grinder and the central re-export hub.

MYS.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Malaysia gross bean imports 490.4 kt — Cote d'Ivoire 102.7, Nigeria 89.4, Ecuador 78.9, Peru 30.4, Cameroon 26.6. Asia's largest grinder; near-zero domestic production.

DEU.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Germany gross bean imports 252.9 kt — Cote d'Ivoire 87.9, Netherlands 56.2 (re-export), Belgium 54.4 (re-export), Cameroon 11.7, Nigeria 11.1, Ghana 10.6. Europe's #2 grinder.

USA.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: US gross bean imports 198.2 kt — Cote d'Ivoire 81.5, Ecuador 52.9, Ghana 31.2, Dominican Republic 18.6, Peru 6.9. Hershey and Mars-Wrigley anchor domestic grinding.

BEL.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Belgium gross bean imports 121.1 kt — Cote d'Ivoire 54.7, Nigeria 18.4, Ghana 16.4, Ecuador 8.3, France 8.0 (re-export). Re-exports ~53% of bean imports; Barry Callebaut (Wieze, world's largest chocolate factory) is the core processor.

TUR.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Turkey gross bean imports 114.5 kt — Cote d'Ivoire 67.7, Cameroon 15.6, Ghana 13.5, Nigeria 5.8. A fast-growing grinder/confectionery hub sourcing almost entirely from West Africa.

FRA.note: ICCO/CBI 2024: France grinds ~150 kt and imports much of its beans via the Netherlands and Belgium hubs, so direct HS-1801 origin imports understate true supply. Second-sourced to ICCO/CBI, not a clean importer-reported bean total.

ESP.note: ICCO/CBI 2024: Spain grinds ~120 kt; like France and Italy it draws much bean supply through NLD/BEL re-export hubs. Figure second-sourced to ICCO/CBI grindings, not a clean importer-reported Comtrade total.

ITA.note: ICCO/CBI 2024: Italy grinds ~100 kt (Ferrero and others) and imports most beans via NLD/BEL. Second-sourced to ICCO/CBI grindings rather than a clean importer-reported bean figure.

CHN.note: ICCO 2024/25: China imports cocoa mainly as semi-finished products and finished chocolate, not raw beans — HS-1801 bean imports negligible. Small emerging Hainan/Yunnan production. Shown via grindings.

JPN.note: ICCO 2024/25: Japan grinds ~50 kt sourced largely from Ghana/West Africa, but direct 2024 HS-1801 reporting is thin (imports more as products). Second-sourced to ICCO grindings.

rankings.note: Exporter ranking is net bean availability (production minus grindings) from ICCO QBCS LI/1 2024/25; Cote d'Ivoire dominates. companies.name: Barry Callebaut
companies.metric: Revenue ~CHF 12.2bn (FY2023/24); sales value jumped on the cocoa-price spike while volumes fell ~3%. World's largest cocoa processor and chocolate manufacturer.
companies.note: Operates the world's largest chocolate factory at Wieze, Belgium, plus major grinding in Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, the Netherlands, Germany, Malaysia. Buys a very large share of the West African crop.
companies.improve: Should publish per-origin verified tonnage and deforestation-free coverage; a large fraction of volume is still bought through traders/cooperatives rather than fully farm-mapped.

companies.name: Cargill Cocoa & Chocolate
companies.metric: Parent Cargill revenue ~US$160bn (FY2024, private); a top-tier global grinder with plants in Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, the Netherlands, Germany.
companies.note: One of the two dominant West-African bean buyers/grinders alongside Barry Callebaut and ofi. Expanded its Yopougon (Abidjan) plant to one of Africa's largest.
companies.improve: Privately held with little segment-level cocoa disclosure; audited origin-share and grinding-capacity reporting would clarify how much of the Ivorian/Ghanaian crop concentrates in one firm.

companies.name: Olam Food Ingredients (ofi)
companies.metric: ofi revenue ~US$15bn (FY2024); cocoa is one of its largest segments, spanning origination, grinding and ingredients.
companies.note: A leading global cocoa originator and processor with deep direct-sourcing in Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana. Runs the AtSource traceability platform.
companies.improve: Should report standalone per-origin verified tonnage rather than bundling cocoa inside group ingredient figures.

companies.name: Mondelez International
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$36bn (FY2024); owner of Cadbury, Milka, Toblerone — one of the largest chocolate buyers of cocoa.
companies.note: Buys liquor/butter/powder and beans via Barry Callebaut, Cargill and ofi. Its Cocoa Life program covers a large share of West-African sourcing.
companies.improve: Relies on third-party processors, so farm-level exposure is one step removed; should publish the share fully Cocoa Life-verified by origin.

companies.name: Nestle
companies.metric: Group revenue ~CHF 91bn (FY2024); KitKat and confectionery make Nestle one of the world's largest cocoa end-users.
companies.note: Sources cocoa products mainly through the major grinders; its Nestle Cocoa Plan and income-accelerator program target Ivorian and Ghanaian farmers.
companies.improve: Should report cocoa volumes fully traceable to farm group by origin, not just a 'responsibly sourced' share.

companies.name: The Hershey Company
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$11.2bn (FY2024); the dominant US chocolate maker and a major buyer of West-African and Ecuadorian beans.
companies.note: Anchors US grinding demand; sources via the major processors with its Cocoa For Good program. Highly exposed to the 2024 price spike.
companies.improve: Should disclose verified farm-traceable tonnage by origin and its direct-vs-trader sourcing split.

global.note: Global cocoa beans, kt, ICCO Quarterly Bulletin of Cocoa Statistics. Production and grindings (consumption proxy) by cocoa year (Oct-Sep): 2023/24 collapsed to ~4489 kt on a severe West-Africa crop failure (~489 kt deficit, driving the historic 2024 price spike to >US$10,000/t), then 2024/25 recovered to ~4840 kt with a small surplus. Exports are raw cocoa-bean trade (HS 1801, ~2.7-3.2 Mt/yr).

forecast.method: OECD-FAO / ICCO envelope; 2030 = 2024×(1+rate)^6. Global cocoa output rising modestly via West-Africa replanting and Ecuador/Latin-America expansion; demand constrained by high prices.
